semin-durr:22-22.t: His saying: {الذين زَعَمْتُمْ}: its first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) is omitted, namely the pronoun referring back (ʿāʾid) to the relative noun, and the second is also omitted, its adjective standing in its place. That is: "you claimed them to be partners besides Allah". It is not permissible for «مِنْ دون» to be the second object, since it does not form a complete statement with what precedes it: if you said «هم من دونِ الله» — that is, without intending a qualified noun — it would not be permissible. And were it not for the adjective standing in its place, it would not be omitted either, because omitting it merely for brevity is rare; moreover, some of them disallowed it altogether.

semin-durr:23-23.t:
His saying: {إِلاَّ لِمَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ}: there are several views on it. The first: that the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the word «الشفاعة» (intercession) itself. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: «as you say: شَفَعْتُ له (I interceded for him)». The second: that it is attached to «تَنْفَعُ»; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. But it is open to objection (fīhi naẓar): it entails one of two things: either the lām is redundant (zāʾida) on the object in a place where it does not belong, or the object of «تنفع» is omitted — and both go against the base rule. The third: that it is an emptied exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh) from the implied object of «الشفاعة», i.e. "intercession will not benefit anyone except the one for whom He permits".
Then the implied "excepted-from" may be the one interceded for — and this is the apparent sense — while the intercessor is not mentioned but only indicated by the purport. The implied meaning is: "intercession will not benefit anyone of those interceded for except one for whom the Exalted has permitted the intercessors to intercede". Or it may be the intercessor, the one interceded for not being mentioned; its implied meaning is: "intercession will not benefit except an intercessor who has been permitted to intercede". On this view, the lām in «له» is the lām of conveyance (lām al-tablīgh), not the lām of cause (lām al-ʿilla). The fourth: that it is also an emptied exception, but from the general states (aḥwāl); its implied meaning is: "intercession will not benefit except being for one for whom He permits". Al-Zamakhsharī set this out, saying: «You say: "الشفاعة لزيدٍ" (the intercession is Zayd's) in the sense that he is the intercessor, as you say "الكَرْمُ لزيدٍ" (generosity is Zayd's); and in the sense that he is the one interceded for, as you say "القيامُ لزيدٍ" (standing up is for Zayd). So His saying {وَلاَ تَنفَعُ الشفاعة عِندَهُ إِلاَّ لِمَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ} may be taken in either of these two senses: i.e. intercession will not benefit except when it belongs to one of the intercessors whom He has permitted and freed for it; or intercession will not benefit except when it is for one for whom He has permitted it, i.e. for his intercessor; or it is the second lām in your saying "أُذِنَ لزيدٍ لعمروٍ" (permission was given to Zayd for ʿAmr), i.e. for his sake — as though it were said: "except for the one for whose sake permission has been given to the intercessor". And this is a subtle view, and it is the right view». End of quote.
So his saying «الكَرْم لزيدٍ» means that it is not the lām of cause but the lām of specification (ikhtiṣāṣ). His saying «القيامُ لزيد» means that it is the lām of cause, as it is in «القيام لزيد». And his saying «أُذن لزيدٍ لعمروٍ» means that the first is for conveyance and the second is the lām of cause.
The two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] and Abū ʿAmr read «أُذِنَ» as passive, the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) being the preposition and its genitive noun. The rest read it active, i.e. "Allah permitted", and that is what is meant in the other reading too. He made it explicit in His sayings: {إِلاَّ مِن بَعْدِ أَن يَأْذَنَ الله} [al-Najm: 26] and {إِلاَّ مَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ الرحمن} [al-Nabaʾ: 38].
His saying: «حتى إذا»: this is a limit (ghāya) which must have something it is the limit of (mughayyā). There are several views about it. The first: that it is His saying {فاتبعوه} [Sabaʾ: 20], on the understanding that the pronoun in «عليهم» of His saying {صَدَّقَ عَلَيْهِمْ} [Sabaʾ: 20] and in «قلوبِهم» refers to all the disbelievers, and the removal of terror (tafzīʿ) is at the moment of departing life; or their following him is made, figuratively, to accompany them until the Day of Resurrection.
And the passage from His saying «قل ادْعُوا» to its end is parenthetical between the limit and what it is the limit of. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] mentioned this, and it is good.
The second: that it is omitted. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: «As though it were said: Nor are they intercessors as you would like; rather they are servants, or submissive, i.e. compliant — until when the terror is removed from their hearts». End of quote. He made the pronoun in «قلوبهم» refer to the angels, established that, and declared weak the view of those who made it refer to the disbelievers or to the whole world; this is not the place to examine that.
His saying «قالوا: ماذا» is the response (jawāb) of «إذا», and His saying «قالوا الحقَّ» is the answer to His saying {مَاذَا قَالَ رَبُّكُمْ}. And «الحقَّ» is accusative by a concealed «قال», i.e. "they said: our Lord said the truth", i.e. the true word. However, the Shaykh rejected this, saying: «What Ibn ʿAṭiyya assumed is not sound, because what follows the limit differs from what precedes it, whereas they are compliant servants always, never ceasing from that — neither when the terror is removed from their hearts nor when it is not removed».
The third: that it is His saying «زَعَمْتُم», i.e. "you claimed disbelief up to the limit of the removal of terror, then you abandoned what you claimed and said: He said the truth". On this view there is iltifāt (grammatical shift) in the speech from the second person in His saying «زَعَمْتم» to the third person in His saying «قلوبهم».
The fourth: that it is what is understood from the context of the speech. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you say: to what is His saying {حتى إِذَا فُزِّعَ} connected, and for what does "حتى" serve as a limit? I say: to what is understood from this speech, namely that there is a waiting for permission, a pausing, a delaying, and fear on the part of those hoping for intercession and of the intercessors as to whether they will be permitted or not; and that permission is not granted except after a long while and a long waiting. This state is indicated by His saying [the Exalted]: {رَّبِّ السماوات} up to His saying {إِلاَّ مَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ الرحمن وَقَالَ صَوَاباً} [al-Nabaʾ: 37-38]. So it is as though it were said: they wait and pause a long while, terrified and alarmed, until when the terror is removed from their hearts — i.e. the terror is lifted from the hearts of the intercessors and those interceded for by a word which the Lord of Might speaks in granting permission — they rejoice at that, and ask one another: What did your Lord say? They say: The truth, i.e. the true word, which is the permission to intercede for whom He is pleased with».
Ibn ʿĀmir read «فَزَّع» as active. If the pronoun in «قلوبهم» is for the angels, then the fāʿil (agent) of «فَزَّع» is a pronoun of the name of Allah the Exalted, because it was mentioned before. And if it is for the disbelievers, then the agent is a pronoun of their misleader. So said the Shaykh. The apparent view is that it refers to Allah in either case. The rest read it passive, the deputy agent being the preposition after it. And faʿʿala with the doubled letter here has the sense of removal (salb), as in قَرَّدْتُ البعيرَ, i.e. "I removed the camel's ticks (qurād)"; likewise here: He removed the terror from them.
Al-Ḥasan read «فُزِعَ» passive and without doubling, like your saying ذُهِب بزيدٍ.
Al-Ḥasan also, Qatāda and Mujāhid read «فَرَّغَ» active, from al-farāgh. Also reported from al-Ḥasan is the undoubled rāʾ; and also from him, and from Ibn ʿUmar and Qatāda, the doubled rāʾ in the passive.
Al-farāgh is annihilation, and the meaning is: until when Allah annihilated the dread, or it vanished by itself, or the dread and fear were removed from their hearts; and when it was made passive, the preposition stood in place of the agent. Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿUmar read «افْرُنْقِعَ», from al-ifrinqāʿ, which is dispersing. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «The word is composed of the letters of al-mufāraqa (separation) with the addition of the ʿayn, just as "اقْمَطَرَّ" is composed of the letters of al-qamṭ with the addition of the rāʾ». The Shaykh said: «If he meant that the ʿayn is one of the letters of augmentation, and likewise the rāʾ — and that is the apparent sense of his words — then it is not correct, because ʿayn and rāʾ are not letters of augmentation. But if he meant that the word contains the letters of what he mentioned, with the ʿayn and the rāʾ in addition, the roots being فَرْقَعَ and قَمْطَر, then it is correct». End of quote. This is a reading that differs from the standard text (al-sawād), and moreover it is a strange word, heavy in pronunciation; the scholars of rhetoric (ahl al-bayān) have explicitly mentioned it and given it as an example. They relate of ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar that he fainted one day and onlookers gathered around him; when he came to, he said: «أراكم تَكَأْكَأْتُمْ عليَّ تَكَأْكُؤَكم على ذي جِنَّةٍ افرَنْقِعوا عني», i.e. "I see you have gathered around me as you would gather around a madman; disperse from me". People faulted him for it, since he used such heavy and strange words.
Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «الحقُّ» in the nominative, as the khabar (predicate) of a concealed mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "they said: His word is the truth".

semin-durr:24-24.t:
His saying: {أَوْ إِيَّاكُمْ}: conjoined to the noun of inna. As for the khabar (predicate), there are several views. The first: that the one pronounced is that of the first, and the predicate of the second is omitted because it is indicated: i.e. "and we are surely upon guidance or in error, or you are surely upon guidance or in error". The second: the reverse, i.e. the first is omitted and the one pronounced is the predicate of the second. This is a well-known disagreement whose detailed examination was given at His saying {والله وَرَسُولُهُ أَحَقُّ أَن يُرْضُوهُ} [al-Tawba: 62]. These two views must by no means be taken at their face value, because the Prophet ﷺ never doubted that he was upon guidance and certainty and that the disbelievers were in error; rather, this speech runs according to the way the Arabs address one another, using fairness in their dialogues by way of supposition and hypothesis. The scholars of rhetoric call it istidrāj (gradual drawing-in): that one mentions to the person addressed something he will concede, even if it is contrary to what one mentions, so that he will listen to what one puts to him; for had he begun with what he dislikes, he would not listen. Similar to it is their saying: "May Allah disgrace whichever of me and you is the liar". Like it is the poet's saying:
3739 - فَأَيِّي ما وأيُّك كان شَرَّاً ... فَقِيْدَ إلى المَقامةِ لا يَرَاها
(Whichever of me and you is the worse, may he be led to the assembly unable to see it.)
And the saying of Ḥassān:
3740 - أَتَهْجُوه ولَسْتَ له بكُفْءٍ ... فَشَرُّكُما لخيرِكما الفِداءُ
(Do you satirise him when you are no match for him? Then may the worse of you two be ransom for the better of you two.)
— though everyone knows that he ﷺ is the best of all Allah's creation.
The third: that it is of the type of al-laff wa-l-nashr (folding and unfolding); the implied meaning is: "and we are surely upon guidance, and you are surely in manifest error". But He folded the two statements together and expressed them thus because there is no ambiguity. This is only possible if «أو» is in the sense of the wāw, which is a matter of disagreement. Of «أو» coming in the sense of the wāw is his saying:
3741 - قَوْمٌ إذا سَمِعوا الصَّرِيْخَ رَأَيْتَهُمْ ... ما بين مُلْجم مُهْره أو سافِعِ
(A people who, when they hear the cry for help, you see them between one bridling his colt and one seizing [its forelock].)
This was set out before, and what I have mentioned is reported from Abū ʿUbayda. The fourth: the Shaykh said: «And "أو" here is in its original meaning, being for one of two things, and the predicate of {إِنَّآ أَوْ إِيَّاكُمْ} is {لعلى هُدًى أَوْ فِي ضَلاَلٍ مُّبِينٍ}, with no need to assume an omission; since the meaning is: one of us is in one of these two — like your saying "Zayd or ʿAmr is in the palace or in the mosque", which needs no assumed omission, since its meaning is: one of these two is in one of these two. And it has been said: the predicate is omitted» — then he mentioned what I gave above to the end. What he mentioned is an explanation of meaning, not an explanation of i'rab; people looked at the explanation of the i'rab, and so they needed what I mentioned.

semin-durr:26-26.t: His saying: {الفتاح العليم}: two intensive adjectives (ṣifatā mubālagha). ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read «الفاتحُ», as an active participle.

semin-durr:27-27.t:
His saying: {أَرُونِيَ}: there are two views on it. The first: that it is the cognitive one (ʿilmiyya), transitive to two objects before the transfer; when the hamza of transfer (hamzat al-naql) was brought, it became transitive to three: the first being the yāʾ of the speaker, the second the relative noun, and the third «شركاءَ»; the pronoun referring back to the relative noun is omitted, i.e. "you joined them to Him". The second: that it is the visual one (baṣariyya), transitive to one object before the transfer and to two after it: the first being the yāʾ of the speaker and the second the relative noun, while «شركاءَ» is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun referring back to the relative noun, i.e. "show me those joined to Him, in the state of being my partners".
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said about this second view: «And there is no use (ghanāʾ) in it», i.e. no benefit in it, meaning that its sense is weak. The Shaykh said: «His saying "there is no use in it" is not good; rather there is in it a rebuke and reproach of them, and He does not intend the literal command; rather the meaning is: those who are My partners according to your claim are such that, if you showed them, you would be disgraced, because they are wood, stone and the like».
His saying: «بل هو»: about this pronoun there are two views. The first: that it is a pronoun referring to Allah the Exalted, i.e. "that One to whom you joined partners is Allah", and «العزيز الحكيم» are two adjectives. The second: that it is the pronoun of the matter and the affair (ḍamīr al-amr wa-l-shaʾn); «الله» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), «العزيز الحكيم» are two predicates, and the clause is the predicate of «هو».

semin-durr:28-28.t:
His saying: {كَآفَّةً}: there are several views on it. The first: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the kāf of «أَرْسَلْناك», the meaning being: "except as one gathering mankind together in the conveying [of the message]".
Al-kāffa has the sense of "the one who gathers together", and the hāʾ in it is for intensiveness (mubālagha), as it is in ʿallāma and rāwiya. Al-Zajjāj said this. This rests on his view that it is an active participle of كَفَّ يَكُفُّ. The Shaykh said: «As for al-Zajjāj's saying that kāffa means "gathering together" and that the hāʾ in it is for intensiveness, the language does not support him in that, because كَفَّ is not attested with the meaning of جَمَعَ (to gather)» — meaning that what is attested for its meaning is "to prevent". One says كَفَّ يَكُفُّ, i.e. he prevented. The meaning [then] is: "except as one preventing them from disbelief and from straying away from your conveying [the message]"; and from it is al-kaff (the palm of the hand), because it prevents what is in it from going out.
The second: that «كافَّة» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) that has come on the pattern fāʿila, like al-ʿāfiya and al-ʿāqiba. On this view, its occurring as a ḥāl is either by way of intensiveness, or by the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "possessed of comprehensiveness for mankind".
The third: that «كافَّة» is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, its implied form being "except with an all-comprehensive sending". Al-Zamakhsharī said: «Except with a sending general to them and encompassing them; because when it includes them all, it prevents (kaffat) any one of them from getting out of it». The Shaykh said: «As for kāffa in the sense of "general", what is reported from the grammarians is that it is only ever a ḥāl and is not used otherwise; so making it an adjective of an omitted maṣdar departs from what they reported; nor is its use as an adjective of an omitted qualified noun attested».
The fourth: that His saying «كافَّةً» is a ḥāl from «للناس», i.e. "to mankind all together". However, al-Zamakhsharī rejected this, saying: «Whoever makes it a ḥāl from the genitive noun, placed before it, has erred; because placing the ḥāl of a genitive noun before it is, in impossibility, on a par with placing the genitive noun before the preposition. How many do you see committing such an error, and then not being content with it until they add to it making the lām mean "to" (ilā); because the first error does not work for him except with the second error, so he has to commit the two errors together». The Shaykh said: «As for what he said, it is a matter of disagreement: the majority held that it is not permissible, while Abū ʿAlī, Ibn Kaysān, Ibn Barhān and Ibn Malkūn held that it is permissible». He said: «And that is the correct view». He said: «Among Abū ʿAlī's examples: "زيدٌ خيرَ ما يكونُ خيرٌ منك" (Zayd, at his best, is better than you), the implied form being "زيدٌ خيرٌ منك خيرَ ما يكونُ", so he made "خيرَ ما يكون" a ḥāl from the kāf in "مِنْكَ" and placed it before it. And he recited:
3742 - إذا المَرْءُ أَعْيَتْه المروءةُ ناشِئاً ... فمطلبُها كهْلاً عليه شديدُ
(When manliness has eluded a man in his youth, then seeking it is hard for him in middle age.)
i.e. "فمطلَبُها عليه كَهْلاً". And he also recited:
3743 - تَسَلَّيْتُ طُرَّاً عنكُمُ بَعْدَ بَيْنِكُمْ ... بذِكْراكمُ حتى كأنَّكُمُ عندي
(I consoled myself entirely about you after your departure by remembering you, until it was as though you were with me.)
i.e. "عنكم طُرَّاً". And the ḥāl has come placed before its genitive possessor and before what it is attached to; he said:
3744 - مَشْغُوفَةً بكِ قد شُغِفْتُ وإنَّما ... حَتَمَ الفراقُ فما إليك سبيلُ
(Smitten with you I have been smitten; but separation has been decreed, so there is no way to you.)
i.e. "قد شُغِفَتْ بك مَشْغوفةً". And another said:
3745 - غافِلاً تَعْرِضُ المنيَّةُ للمَرْ ... ءِ فيُدْعَى ولات حينَ إباءُ
(Death comes upon a man while he is heedless, and he is summoned, and it is no time for refusing.)
i.e. "death comes upon a man heedless"». He said: «And if it is permissible to place it before its possessor and before what governs it, then placing it before its possessor alone is all the more permissible». He said: «Among those who took it as a ḥāl is Ibn ʿAṭiyya, for he said: "It was placed first for emphasis"; and what is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās is his saying: "To the Arabs, the non-Arabs and all the nations", its implied form being "to mankind all together"». He said: «As for al-Zamakhsharī's saying "the first error does not work for him…" etc., it is outrageous; because one who holds that view does not need to make the lām mean "to", since أَرْسَلَ is made transitive with the lām; the Exalted said: {وَأَرْسَلْنَاكَ لِلنَّاسِ رَسُولاً} [al-Nisāʾ: 79]; and "أرسلَ" is among the verbs made transitive with the lām and also with "إلى". And the lām has come in the sense of "إلى", and "إلى" in its sense».
I say: as for {أَرْسَلْنَاكَ لِلنَّاسِ}, there is no evidence in it, since the lām may be the lām of figurative cause. And as for its being in the sense of «إلى» and the reverse, the Basrans do not allow figurative use in particles. And «بشيراً ونذيراً» are also two ḥāls.

semin-durr:30-30.t:
His saying: {لَّكُم مِّيعَادُ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). As for «الميعاد», several views are possible. The first: that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) put in construct with its adverb of time; and al-mīʿād is applied to both al-waʿd (promise) and al-waʿīd (threat). It was mentioned before that al-waʿd is for good and al-waʿīd for evil, mostly. The second: a noun put in the place of the maṣdar. The apparent view is the first. Abū ʿUbayda said: «al-waʿd, al-waʿīd and al-mīʿād have one meaning». The third: that here it is an adverb of time. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «Al-mīʿād is the container of the promise, whether of place or time, and here it is an adverb of time. The evidence for this is the reading of whoever read "ميعادٌ يومٌ"» — meaning both in the nominative with tanwīn — «so "اليوم" was made a badal (substitute) from it. As for the construct, it is a construct of clarification (iḍāfat tabyīn), like your saying "سَحْقُ ثوبٍ" (a worn-out garment) and "بعيرُ سانِيَةٍ" (a camel for drawing water)».
The Shaykh said: «What he said is not the only possibility, since the implied form may be "لكم ميعادُ ميعادِ يومٍ"; when the muḍāf was omitted, the muḍāf ilayhi took its case». I say: had al-Zamakhsharī done the like, he would have publicised it [against him]. Al-Zamakhsharī allowed another view for the nominative: the nominative of magnification (al-raf ʿalā al-taʿẓīm), i.e. with an implied mubtadaʾ; this is what is called al-qaṭʿ (severing). This will come shortly.
Ibn Abī ʿAbla and al-Yazīdī read «ميعادٌ يوماً», with tanwīn on the first and «يوماً» accusative with tanwīn. There are two views on it. The first: that it is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), governed by an implied muḍāf, its implied form being: "for you is the fulfilment of a promise on a day whose description is such and such". The second: that it is accusative by an implied verb. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «As for the accusative of "اليوم", it is by way of magnification, with an implied verb, its implied form being "I mean a day". And the nominative may also be on this basis, I mean magnification».
ʿĪsā read with tanwīn on the first and «يوم» accusative, put in construct with the clause after it. In it are the two views mentioned before: accusative of magnification, or adverb.
His saying: {لاَّ تَسْتَأْخِرُونَ عَنْهُ}: this clause may be an adjective of «مِيْعاد» if the pronoun in «عنه» refers to it, or of «يوم» if the pronoun in «عنه» refers to it; so its position may be judged nominative or genitive. As for ʿĪsā's reading, the pronoun in «عنه» should refer to «ميعاد» only; because they have stated explicitly that when an adverb is put in construct with a clause, no pronoun returns from that clause to it except in poetic necessity, as in his saying:
3746 - مَضَتْ سَنَةٌ لِعامَ وُلِدْتُ فيه ... وعَشْرٌ بعد ذاكَ وحِجَّتانِ
(A year has passed since the year I was born in, and ten after that, and two pilgrimage-years.)

semin-durr:31-31.t:
His saying: {وَلَوْ تَرَى ا}: the object of «ترى» and the response (jawāb) of «لو» are both omitted because they are understood; i.e. "if you could see the state of the wrongdoers at the time of their standing, some of them throwing back words at others, you would see a terrible state and a hideous affair". «يَرْجِعُ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of «مَوْقوفون», and «القول» is accusative by «يَرْجِعُ», because it is transitive; the Exalted said: {فَإِن رَّجَعَكَ الله} [al-Tawba: 83]. His saying {يَقُولُ الذين استضعفوا} to its end is an explication of His saying «يَرْجِعُ», so it has no grammatical position. «أنتم» after «لولا» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) according to the soundest of the doctrines. This — I mean the occurrence of nominative pronouns after «لولا» — is the most eloquent usage, contrary to al-Mubarrad, who considered the opposite of this a solecism (laḥn), and held that it occurred only in the saying of Yazīd:
3747 - وكم مَوْطَنٍ لَوْلاي. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(How many a place where, had it not been for me…)
— the verse. Its examination was given before. Al-Akhfash held that it is an accusative or genitive pronoun standing in place of the nominative pronoun, and Sībawayh held it to be a genitive pronoun.

semin-durr:33-33.t:
His saying: {بَلْ مَكْرُ الليل}: its nominative may be explained in three ways. The first: as fāʿil (agent), its implied form being "rather your plotting in these two times turned us away". The second: that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. "the plotting of the night turned us away". The third: the reverse, i.e. "the cause of our disbelief is your plotting". The construct of «المَكْر» with the night and the day is either by figurative attribution (isnād majāzī), as in their saying "a plotting night", so that it is a maṣdar put in construct with its nominative [agent]; or by extension (ittisāʿ) in the adverb, so that it is treated like a direct object, and thus it is put in construct with its accusative. These two are better than the view of whoever said that the construct is in the sense of «في», i.e. "in the night", because that has not been established outside the point in dispute.
The generality (al-ʿāmma) read «مَكْرُ» with an undoubled rāʾ and a quiescent kāf, in construct with what follows it. Ibn Yaʿmar and Qatāda read «مكرٌ» with tanwīn, and «الليل» and «النهار» accusative as two adverbs. He also, and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Abū Ruzayn, read it with a fatḥa on the kāf and a doubled rāʾ, in construct with what follows it, i.e. "the recurring (kurūr) of the night and the day and their alternation", from كَرَّ يَكُرُّ, when something comes and goes. Ibn Jubayr also, Ṭalḥa, and Rāshid the reciter — he who used to correct the muṣḥafs in the days of al-Ḥajjāj by his order — read it likewise, except with the rāʾ in the accusative. There are several views on this. The most apparent is what al-Zamakhsharī said, namely accusative as a maṣdar (absolute object); he said: «Rather you repeat the leading astray, a perpetual repetition, never slackening from it». The second: accusative as an adverb, with an implied verb, i.e. "rather you turned us away throughout the recurrence of night and day", i.e. constantly. The third: that it is accusative by «تَأْمُرُوننا»; Abū al-Faḍl al-Rāzī said this, and it is a mistake, because what comes after the muḍāf does not govern what precedes it, except in one case, namely «غير» when it is in the sense of «لا», as in his saying:
3748 - إنَّ أمْرَأً خَصَّني عَمْداً مَوَدَّتَه ... على التَّنائي لَعِندي غيرُ مَكْفورِ
(A man who deliberately singled me out for his affection despite the distance is, with me, not one whose favour is denied.)
The explanation of this was given at the end of al-Fātiḥa.
His saying {قَالَ الذين استكبروا} came without a conjunction because it is an answer to the words of the weak, so it was made a new start (istiʾnāf); unlike His saying {وَقَالَ الذين استضعفوا}, for since it was not an answer, it was conjoined. The pronoun in «وأَسَرُّوا الندامةَ» is for all of them: the followers and the followed.

semin-durr:34-34.t:
His saying: {إِلاَّ قَالَ مُتْرَفُوهَآ}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause from «قرية», even though it is indefinite, because it is in the context of negation.
His saying: «بما أُرْسِلْتُمْ»: attached to the khabar (predicate) of «إنَّ», and «به» is attached to «أُرْسِلْتُمْ». The implied form is: "we are disbelievers in that with which you have been sent". It was placed first only for emphasis, and the matching of the verse-endings (fawāṣil) made it fitting.

semin-durr:36-36.t: His saying: {وَيَقْدِرُ}: i.e. He straitens, as shown by its being set against «يَبْسُط». This is the rhetorical ṭibāq (antithesis). Al-Aʿmash read «ويُقَدِّر» with doubling in both places.

semin-durr:37-37.t:
His saying: {بالتي تُقَرِّبُكُمْ}: an adjective of «الأموال» and «الأولاد», because a broken plural of non-rational beings is treated like a singular feminine. Al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj said that He omitted from the first because the second indicates it; they said: the implied form is "your wealth is not that which brings you near to Us in nearness, nor are your children that which brings you near". This too is unnecessary. And it is reported from al-Farrāʾ, as mentioned before, that «التي» is an adjective of the wealth and the children together; and this is the correct view. Al-Zamakhsharī made «التي» an adjective of an omitted qualified noun. He said: «And it may be piety (al-taqwā), which alone is what brings near to Allah in nearness, i.e. your wealth and your children are not that which is described, with Allah, as bringing near». The Shaykh said: «There is no need for this qualified noun». I say: in relation to the meaning he mentioned, the need for it is compelling.
His saying: «زُلْفَى»: a maṣdar (verbal noun) from the meaning of the first [verb], since the implied form is "brings you near a nearness". Al-Ḍaḥḥāk read «زُلَفاً», with a fatḥa on the lām and tanwīn on the word, as the plural of zulfā, like qurba and qurab; the maṣdar was put in the plural because of the variety of its kinds.
His saying: {إِلاَّ مَنْ آمَنَ}: there are several views on it. The first: that it is a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), so it is accusative in position. The second: that it is in the position of the genitive, as a badal (substitute) from the pronoun in «أموالكم»; al-Zajjāj said this. Al-Naḥḥās faulted him because it is a substitute from the pronoun of the person addressed. He said: «If this were permissible, then "رَأَيْتُك زيداً" would be permissible. And this view of Abū Isḥāq is the view of al-Farrāʾ». End of quote.
The Shaykh said: «The doctrine of al-Akhfash and the Kufans is that substitution from the pronoun of the addressee and the speaker is permissible; however, substitution in the verse is not sound. Do you not see that it is not sound to empty (tafrīgh) the verb occurring as a ṣila (relative clause) for what follows "إلاَّ"? If you said "ما زيدٌ بالذي يَضْرِب إلاَّ خالداً", it would not be permissible. Al-Zajjāj imagined that, since the ṣila is negated in meaning, substitution is permissible; but it is not permissible unless emptying is sound for it». I say: his disallowing your saying «ما زيدٌ بالذي يَضْرب إلاَّ خالداً» is open to objection, because when the negation extends over the whole clause, it is given the same rule as if it directly governed that thing. Do you not see that the negation in your saying «ما ظننتُ أحداً يَفْعلُ ذلك إلاَّ زيدٌ» permitted the substitution of «زيد» from the pronoun of «يَفْعَل», even though the negation was not directly over it? They said: but since it was within the scope of negation, that was sound in it; and this is like it.
Al-Zamakhsharī also followed al-Zajjāj and al-Farrāʾ in this as regards the meaning, except that he did not make it a substitute but accusative on the basis of ordinary exception. He said: «"إلاَّ مَنْ آمنَ" is an exception from the "كم" in "تُقَرِّبُكم". The meaning is: wealth does not bring anyone near except the believer who spends it in the way of Allah; and children do not bring anyone near except one who taught them good, gave them understanding of the religion and prepared them for righteousness».
The Shaykh answered him with something like what preceded, saying: «It is not permissible to say "ما زيدٌ بالذي يَخْرُج إلاَّ أخوه" or "ما زيدٌ بالذي يَضْرب إلاَّ عَمْراً"». The reply to this is what preceded; moreover, al-Zamakhsharī did not make it a substitute but an explicit exception, and exception does not require verbal emptying but [only] semantic attribution. Do you not see that you say «قام القومُ إلاَّ زيداً», whereas if you emptied it verbally it would be impossible, because it is affirmative? This which al-Zamakhsharī mentioned is the third view in the matter.
The fourth: that «مَنْ آمَنَ» is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is His saying {فأولئك لَهُمْ جَزَآءُ الضعف}. Al-Farrāʾ said: «It is in a nominative position, its implied form being: none is the one brought near except whoever believes». This has nothing to it, and I wonder how al-Farrāʾ could say it.
The generality read «جزاءُ الضِّعْفِ» in construct, as a maṣdar put in construct with its object, i.e. "that He should recompense them the double". Al-Zamakhsharī assumed it as passive, i.e. "they are recompensed the double". The Shaykh rejected this on the ground that the correct view is to disallow it. Qatāda read both in the nominative, with «الضِّعْف» as a substitute from «جزاء». Also from him and from Yaʿqūb [is the reading] «جزاءً» in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), governed by the [notion of] being established (al-istiqrār); this is like His saying {فَلَهُ جَزَآءً الحسنى} [al-Kahf: 88] according to whoever read «جزاء» in the accusative in al-Kahf.
His saying: «في الغُرُفاتِ»: Ḥamza read «الغُرْفَة» in the singular, intending the genus and because there is no ambiguity, since it is known that each person has a chamber of his own. There is agreement on the singular in His saying {يُجْزَوْنَ الغرفة} [al-Furqān: 75]; and because the singular form is lighter, so it was put in place of the plural when ambiguity is safely absent. The rest read «الغُرُفات», a sound plural. There is agreement on the plural in His saying {لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهُمْ مِّنَ الجنة غُرَفَاً} [al-ʿAnkabūt: 58]. The script allows both readings. Al-Ḥasan read the rāʾ of «غُرُفات» with a ḍamma by assimilation (itbāʿ), and some give it a fatḥa; the examination of this was given at the beginning of al-Baqara. Ibn Waththāb read «الغُرُفَة» with a ḍamma on the rāʾ and in the singular.

semin-durr:39-39.t:
His saying: {وَمَآ أَنفَقْتُمْ}: «ما» may be a relative noun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is His saying «فهو يُخْلِفُه»; the fāʾ entered because of its resemblance to a condition. And «مِنْ شَيْءٍ» is explicative (bayān) — so it was said. But this is open to objection, because of the vagueness of «شيء»: what clarification is there in it? The second: that it is conditional, and so in the position of the accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and «فهو يُخْلِفُه» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).
His saying: «الرازِقين»: it was put in the plural only with regard to outward form, because a person provides for his dependants out of the provision of Allah, whereas the true Provider for all is only Allah the Exalted.

semin-durr:40-40.t:
His saying: {وَيَوْمَ يَحْشُرُهُمْ جَمِيعاً ثُمَّ يَقُولُ}: it was mentioned before, in al-Anʿām, that it is read with the nūn and with the yāʾ.
His saying: {أهؤلاء إِيَّاكُمْ كَانُواْ يَعْبُدُونَ}: «إيَّاكم» is accusative by the khabar (predicate) of kāna; it was placed first for the sake of the verse-endings (fawāṣil) and for emphasis. It has been adduced as evidence for the permissibility of placing the predicate of «كان» before it when its predicate is a clause, for there is disagreement about this: Ibn al-Sarrāj permitted it, and others disallowed it. Likewise they disagreed about placing it in the middle when it is a clause; Ibn al-Sarrāj said: «Analogy requires its permissibility, but it has not been heard». I say: it was mentioned before at His saying {مَا كَانَ يَصْنَعُ فِرْعَوْنُ} [al-Aʿrāf: 137] and the like that it may be a case of placing the predicate first, and may not. The point of the evidence here is that placing the governed word (maʿmūl) first signals [the permissibility of] placing the governing word (ʿāmil) first. The examination of this, and the rejection of this rule, were given in Hūd at His saying {أَلاَ يَوْمَ يَأْتِيهِمْ لَيْسَ مَصْرُوفاً} [Hūd: 8].

semin-durr:42-42.t: His saying: {التي كُنتُم بِهَا}: an adjective of «النار», whereas in al-Sajda it is an adjective of «العذاب». It was said: because there they were involved in the punishment and going to and fro in it, so what they were involved in was described for them; whereas here they have not yet come into contact with it, because it comes right after their being gathered.

semin-durr:44-44.t:
His saying: {يَدْرُسُونَهَا}: the generality (al-ʿāmma) read it without doubling, the imperfect of the undoubled درس, i.e. "he memorised". Abū Ḥaywa read «يَدَّرِسُوْنَها», with a fatḥa on the doubled dāl and a kasra on the rāʾ; the original form is يَدْتَرِسُوْنها, from al-iddirās on the pattern iftiʿāl, and it was assimilated. Also from him: with a ḍamma on the yāʾ, a fatḥa on the dāl and a doubled rāʾ, from al-tadrīs.
His saying: {وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا إِلَيْهِمْ قَبْلَكَ}: i.e. to these contemporaries of yours We did not send any warner other than you to address them directly with warning. So there is no contradiction between it and His saying {وَإِن مِّنْ أُمَّةٍ إِلاَّ خَلاَ فِيهَا نَذِيرٌ} [Fāṭir: 24], since what is meant there is the traces of the warner; and there is no doubt that this existed: the prophet departs and his law remains.

semin-durr:45-45.t:
His saying: {وَمَا بَلَغُواْ}: the apparent view is that the pronoun in «بَلَغُوا» and in «آتيناهم» is for those before them, so as to accord with His saying «فكذَّبُوا رُسُلي»; the meaning being that they did not attain, in gratitude for the blessing and in requiting the favour, a tenth (miʿshār) of what We gave them of blessings and kindness to them. And it was said: rather the nominative pronoun is for Quraysh and the accusative for those before them; this is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās, in the sense that they [the earlier ones] had more wealth. And it was said: the reverse, in the sense: We gave Quraysh signs and proofs such as We did not give those before them.
There is disagreement about al-miʿshār. It was said: it means al-ʿushr (a tenth); the pattern mifʿāl was formed from the word ʿushr, like al-mirbāʿ (a quarter), and there is no third like them among number words: one does not say misdās or mikhmās. And it was said: it is a tenth of a tenth. But Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejected this and said: «It is nothing». Al-Māwardī said: «Al-miʿshār here is a tenth of al-ʿushayr, and al-ʿushayr is a tenth of a tenth, so it is one part in a thousand». He said: «And this is the most apparent, because what is meant by it is extreme diminution».
His saying: «فَكَذَّبوا»: there are two views on it. The first: that it is conjoined to {كَذَّبَ الَّذِينَ مِن قَبلِهِمْ}. The second: that it is conjoined to «وما بَلَغُوا». Al-Zamakhsharī explained both, saying: «If you say: what is the meaning of "فكذَّبُوا رُسُلي", when it is dispensed with by His saying {وَكَذَّبَ الَّذِينَ مِن قَبلِهِمْ}? I say: since the meaning of His saying {وَكَذَّبَ الَّذِينَ مِن قَبلِهِمْ} is "those before them committed denial and ventured upon it", the denial of the messengers was made a consequence of it. Similar to it is someone saying: "So-and-so ventured upon disbelief, and so he disbelieved in Muhammad ﷺ". And it may be conjoined to His saying "وما بَلَغوا", as in your saying: "Zayd did not attain a tenth of ʿAmr's excellence, so he [ʿAmr] surpassed him"».
And «نَكير» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) put in construct with its agent, i.e. "My disapproval". The omission and retention of its yāʾ were discussed before.

semin-durr:46-46.t:
His saying: {أَن تَقُومُواْ}: there are several views on it. The first: that it is genitive in position as a badal (substitute) from «واحدة», by way of clarification; al-Fārisī said this. The second: that it is an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) of «واحدة»; al-Zamakhsharī said this. It is rejected because the two differ in definiteness and indefiniteness; this was discussed before at His saying {فِيهِ آيَاتٌ بَيِّنَاتٌ مَّقَامُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ} [Āl ʿImrān: 97]. The third: that it is accusative by an implied «أعني» (I mean). The fourth: that it is nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "it is that you stand". And «مَثْنى» and «فُرادى» are a ḥāl (circumstantial). The examination of «مَثْنى» and its class was given in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ, and the discussion of «فُرادى» in Sūrat al-Anʿām.
His saying: «ثم تتفَكَّروا»: conjoined to «أَنْ تَقُوموا», i.e. "your standing, then your reflecting".
According to Abū Ḥātim the pause is at this [point of the] verse, and then one begins «ما بصاحبِكم». About this «ما» there are two views. The first: that it is negative. The second: that it is interrogative, but the real sense of interrogation is not intended, so it comes back to negation. If it is negative, is it suspending (muʿalliqa) [the verb], or a new start (mustaʾnafa), or the answer to an oath implied in the meaning of «تَتَفَكَّروا», since it is a verb of ascertainment like تبيَّن and its class? Three views. Ibn ʿAṭiyya reported the third, and perhaps ascribed it to Sībawayh. If it is interrogative, the first two views are permissible in it, but not the third. And «مِنْ جِنَّةٍ» may be a fāʿil (agent) of the preposition-phrase, because it is supported [by a preceding negation], or it may be a mubtadaʾ. And «ما», if negative, may be the Ḥijāzī or the Tamīmī [kind].

semin-durr:47-47.t: His saying: {مَا سَأَلْتُكُم}: there are two views about «ما». The first: that it is conditional, and so it is a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and «فهو لكم» is its apodosis (jawāb). The second: that it is a relative noun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), the pronoun referring back being omitted, i.e. "[what] I asked you for it"; and the khabar (predicate) is «فهو لكم». The [fāʾ] entered because of the resemblance of the relative to a condition. The meaning may be that he did not ask them for any wage at all, as in your saying «If you have given me anything, take it», while you know that he gave you nothing; and this is supported by {إِنْ أَجْرِيَ إِلاَّ عَلَى الله}. Or it may be that he asked them for something whose benefit returns to them, which is what is meant by His saying {إِلاَّ المودة فِي القربى} [al-Shūrā: 23].

semin-durr:48-48.t:
His saying: {يَقْذِفُ بالحق}: its object may be omitted, because al-qadhf originally means throwing, and here it is used to express casting, i.e. "He casts the revelation to His prophets with the truth", i.e. because of the truth, or bound up with the truth. Or the implied form may be: "He hurls falsehood with the truth", i.e. repels it and casts it down with it, as in His saying {بَلْ نَقْذِفُ بالحق عَلَى الباطل} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 18]. Or the bāʾ may be redundant (zāʾida), i.e. "He casts the truth", as in His saying {وَلاَ تُلْقُواْ بِأَيْدِيكُمْ} [al-Baqara: 195]; or «يقْذِفُ» is made to include (tuḍammanu) the meaning of "He decrees and judges".
His saying: «عَلاَّمُ الغيوبِ»: the generality read it in the nominative. There are several views on it, the most apparent: that it is a second khabar (predicate) of «إنَّ»; or the predicate of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject); or a badal (substitute) from the pronoun in «يَقْذِفُ»; or a naʿt (adjective) of it according to the opinion of al-Kisāʾī, because he permits qualifying the third-person pronoun, and he stated it explicitly here. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «Nominative on the position of "إنَّ" and its noun, or on the latent pronoun in "يَقْذِفُ"». I say: by his saying «carried on the position of inna and its noun» he means the adjective; but that is not the doctrine of the Basrans, who did not take the position into account except in conjunction by a particle, with conditions according to some of them. And by carrying it on the pronoun in «يَقْذِفُ» he means that it is a substitute from it, not an adjective of it, because the latter is held by al-Kisāʾī alone. Zayd ibn ʿAlī, ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and Ibn Abī Isḥāq [read it] in the accusative, as an adjective of the noun of «إنَّ», or a substitute from it — though substitution with a derived word is rare — or accusative as praise (al-madḥ).
And «الغيوبِ» has been read with all three vowels on the ghayn. The kasra and the ḍamma were discussed before at «بيوت» and its class; as for the fatḥa, it is an intensive form like al-shakūr and al-ṣabūr, and it is the absent thing that is extremely hidden.

semin-durr:49-49.t:
His saying: {وَمَا يُبْدِىءُ}: «ما» may be negative, or it may be interrogative, but its meaning comes back to negation. There is no object for «يُبْدِئُ» nor for «يُعِيْد», since what is meant is: he does not perform these two acts, as in his saying:
3749 - أَقْفَرَ مِنْ أهلِه عبيدُ ... أصبحَ لا يُبْدِيْ ولا يُعيدُ
(ʿUbayd has become empty of his people; he has come to neither begin nor repeat.)
And it was said: its object is omitted, i.e. "it does not bring forth good for its people at first nor bring it back"; this is al-Ḥasan's assumed form.

semin-durr:50-50.t:
His saying: {إِن ضَلَلْتُ}: the generality (al-ʿāmma) read it with a fatḥa on its lām in the past tense and a kasra in the imperfect, though it is transferred to the quiescent letter before it. Al-Ḥasan and Ibn Waththāb read the reverse, which is the dialect of Tamīm; this was discussed before.
His saying: «فبما يُوْحِي»: [«ما»] may be maṣdariyya (verbal-noun-forming), i.e. "because of my Lord's revealing to me", or a relative noun, i.e. "because of that which He reveals", its pronoun referring back being omitted.

semin-durr:51-51.t:
His saying: {فَلاَ فَوْتَ}: the generality read it as indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and «أُخِذُوا» as a passive past verb, conjoined to «فَزِعُوا». And it was said: [conjoined] to the meaning of «فلا فَوْتَ», i.e. "so they did not escape, and they were seized".
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, the client of Banū Hāshim, and Ṭalḥa read «فلا فَوْتٌ» and «أَخْذٌ», both nominative with tanwīn; and Ubayy [read] «فَوْت» with a fatḥa and «أَخْذ» in the nominative. The nominative of «فَوْت» is as a mubtadaʾ (subject), or as the noun of the «لا» that functions like laysa. Whoever read «وأَخْذٌ» in the nominative made it nominative as a mubtadaʾ with an omitted khabar (predicate), i.e. "and there is seizing there", or as the predicate of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "and their state is seizing"; and it is then a conjunction of clauses, an affirmative one conjoined to a negative one.

semin-durr:52-52.t:
And the pronoun in «آمنَّا به» is for Allah the Exalted, or for the Messenger, or for the Qurʾān, or for the punishment, or for the resurrection.
His saying: «التَّناوُشُ»: a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «أنَّى» is its khabar (predicate), i.e. "how can they have the reaching?"; and «لهم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial). Or «لهم» may make «التناوش» nominative [as its agent], because it is supported by the interrogative, its implied form being: "how is the reaching established for them?" — but this is far-fetched. «التناؤش» is with a hamza in the reading of the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī], Abū ʿAmr and Abū Bakr, and with a wāw in the reading of the others. So the two may be independent roots with the same meaning. And it was said: the hamza is from the wāw because it carries a ḍamma, like wujūh and ujūh, wuqqitat and uqqitat. A large group held this, such as al-Zajjāj, al-Zamakhsharī, Ibn ʿAṭiyya, al-Ḥawfī and Abū al-Baqāʾ. Al-Zajjāj said: «Every wāw carrying a necessary ḍamma, you have the choice regarding it», and the rest followed him in wording close to his. The Shaykh rejected this generalisation and restricted it: the wāw must not be one into which [another wāw] is assimilated — to exclude al-taʿawwudh — and it must not be kept sound (muṣaḥḥaḥa) in the verb; for whenever it is kept sound in the verb it is not changed to a hamza, as in tarahwaka tarahwukan and taʿāwana taʿāwunan. With this last restriction their view is void, because it is kept sound in tanāwasha yatanāwashu; and once these two restrictions, or the last of them, are granted to him, his rejection holds.
Al-tanāwush is returning, and it was recited:
3750 - تَمَنَّى أَنْ تَؤُوْبَ إليَّ مَيٌّ ... وليس إلى تناوُشِها سبيلُ
(He wishes that Mayy would come back to me, but there is no way to her returning.)
i.e. to her returning. And it was said: it is taking (al-tanāwul); one says ناشَ كذا, i.e. he took it. And from it is: the people reached at one another with weapons, as in his saying:
3751 - ظَلَّتْ سُيوفُ بني أَبيه تَنُوْشُه ... للهِ أرحام هناك تُشَقَّقُ
(The swords of his father's sons kept reaching at him — by Allah, what ties of kinship are being torn there!)
And another said:
3752 - فَهْيَ تَنُوْشُ الحَوْضَ نَوْشاً مِنْ عَلا ... نَوْشاً به تَقْطَعُ أجوازَ الفَلا
(She reaches at the trough from above, a reaching by which she crosses the midst of the deserts.)
And some distinguished between the hamzated form and the other, making the one with hamza mean lateness. Al-Farrāʾ said: «From نَأَشْتُ, i.e. I was late». And he recited:
3753 - تَمَنَّى نَئِيْشاً أَنْ يكونُ مُطاعِناً ... وقد حَدَثَتْ بعد الأمورِ أمورُ
(He wished, belatedly, that he were a fighter with the spear, when after events other events had come about.)
And another said:
3754 - قَعَدْتَ زماناً عن طِلابك للعُلا ... وجِئْتَ نَئيشاً بعد ما فاتَكَ الخبرُ
(You sat back for a time from seeking high rank, and came belatedly after the news had passed you by.)
Al-Farrāʾ also said: «They are close to each other» — meaning the hamza and its omission — «like ذِمْتُ الرجلَ and ذَأََمْتُه, i.e. I found fault with him». And انتاش انتِياشاً is like تَناوَشَ تناوُشاً. He said:
3755 - باتَتْ تَنُوْشُ العَنَقَ انْتِياشاً
(She spent the night reaching out at a brisk pace.)
This is a maṣdar on a different pattern from the verb. And «مِنْ مكانٍ» is attached to «التَّناوش».

semin-durr:53-53.t:
His saying: {وَقَدْ كَفَرُواْ}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause, and «مِنْ قبلُ» means: before the removal of the punishment. Or the clause may be resumptive (mustaʾnafa); the first is more apparent.
His saying: «ويَقْذِفُون»: it may be resumptive, or a ḥāl; but the latter is far-fetched — the reverse of the former case — because the wāw enters on an affirmative imperfect. The pronoun in «به» is as discussed before regarding it after «آمنَّا». Abū Ḥaywa, Mujāhid, and Maḥbūb from Abū ʿAmr read «يُقْذَفون» as passive, i.e. "they are pelted with what grieves them, as a result of their deeds, from where they do not expect".

semin-durr:54-54.t:
His saying: {وَحِيلَ}: the ishmām (blending of the vowel) and the kasra in it were discussed at the beginning of al-Baqara. The nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is the pronoun of the maṣdar, i.e. "and it was interposed", i.e. the interposing (al-ḥawl). Do not assume it to be an emphatic maṣdar but a specified one, so that its standing [as deputy agent] is sound. Al-Ḥawfī made «بينهم» the deputy agent, and it was objected against him that it should then have been nominative. It was answered that it was made indeclinable on the fatḥa only because it is put in construct with an undeclinable word. The Shaykh rejected this on the ground that a muḍāf put in construct with an undeclinable word is not made indeclinable absolutely; so one may not say «قام غلامَك» nor «مررتُ بغلامَك» with the fatḥa. I say: what was mentioned before at His saying {لَقَد تَّقَطَّعَ بَيْنَكُمْ} [al-Anʿām: 94] spares us repeating it here. Then the Shaykh said: «And what does the one who says that say about the poet's saying:
3756 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وقد حِيْلَ بين العَيْرِ والنَّزَوانِ
(…and a barrier was set between the wild ass and its leaping.)
For he put "بين" in the accusative while in construct with a declinable word. On the same basis the saying of the other was also explained:
3757 - وقالَتْ متى يُبْخَلُ عليك ويُعْتَلَلْ ... يَسُؤْكَ وإن يُكشَفْ غرامُك تَدْرَبِ
(She said: whenever there is stinginess towards you and excuses are made, it will grieve you; and if your passion is exposed, you will grow used to it.)
i.e. يُعْتَلَلْ هو, i.e. the excusing».
His saying: «مِنْ قبلُ»: attached to «فُعِل», or to «بأشياعهم», i.e. those who sided with them before that time.
His saying: «مُريب»: it was mentioned before that it is an active participle of أراب, i.e. he brought about doubt (rayb), or entered into it; and أَرَبْتُه means "I made him fall into doubt". Attributing the causing of doubt to doubt is figurative. Al-Zamakhsharī said here: «Except that here there is a slight difference: al-murīb from the transitive [verb] is transferred from what can properly be causing doubt — among concrete beings — to the abstract notion; and from the intransitive it is transferred from the one having doubt to the doubt, as you say: "a poetic poem" (shiʿrun shāʿir)». This is a fine and useful expression. How far is this from the saying of some of them: «He may have made it follow "doubt" so that the end of the verse accords with the one before it, "مِنْ مكانٍ قريبٍ"»; and from Ibn ʿAṭiyya's saying: «Al-murīb is the strongest and most severe doubt». The examination of al-rayb was given at the beginning of al-Baqara, together with al-Rāghib's censure of whoever explains it as doubt (shakk).

semin-durr:1-1.t:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

His saying: {الذي لَهُ}: it may be a follower (as an adjective), or it may be cut off, in the accusative or the nominative, for praise in both cases. And {مَا فِي السماوات} may be the agent of «له» (the preposition and its genitive noun, which is the better view), or it may be a mubtadaʾ.

His saying: «في الآخرةِ»: it may be attached to the ḥamd (praise) itself, or attached to what its khabar is attached to. «وهو الحكيمُ» may be parenthetical, if we parse «يَعْلَمُ» as a confirmatory ḥāl from the pronoun of the Creator, the Exalted; and «يَعْلَمُ» may be resumptive, or a ḥāl from the pronoun in «الخبير».

semin-durr:2-2.t: His saying: {وَمَا يَنزِلُ}: the majority read «يَنْزِلُ» with fatḥa on the yāʾ and the zāy unshadded, attributed to the pronoun of «ما». ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, and al-Sulamī read it with ḍamma and a shadda on the zāy, that is: Allah the Exalted (sends it down).

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying: {بلى}: an answer to their saying «لا تَأْتينا» ("it will not come to us"), and what follows it is an oath upon that. The majority read «لَتَأْتِيَنَّكم» in the feminine. Ṭalq read it with a yāʾ, and it was said: that is, the resurrection (al-baʿth).

It was also said: it is according to the meaning of the Hour, that is: "the day". al-Zamakhsharī said this. The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) rejected it as a poetic necessity, like the saying:

3710 - ... nor a land that has sprouted its sprouting (... ولا أَرْضَ أبْقَلَ إبْقالَها)

and it is not like it. It was also said: that is, Allah, in the sense of His command. By analogy with this explanation, «عالمُ» may be the agent of «يَأْتَيَنَّكم» in the reading of one who made it nominative.

His saying: «عالم»: the two (al-Akhawān, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) read «عَلاّم» in the intensive form, and genitive as an adjective of «رَبِّي», or a badal of it, which is rare because it is derived. Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read «عالمُ» nominative, as "he is the Knower", or as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is «لا يَعْزُب», or because its khabar is implied, that is "he"; al-Ḥawfī mentioned it, and there is remoteness in it. The rest read «عالم» genitive, as stated. And if it is made an adjective, its definiteness must be implied. It has already been mentioned that every adjective may be made definite by iḍāfa except the resembling adjective (al-ṣifa al-mushabbaha). The two readings of «يَعْزُب» were given in Sūrat Yūnus.

His saying: «ولا أَصْغَرُ»: the majority read «أصغر» and «أكبر» nominative. There are two explanations. The first: it is a mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is {إِلاَّ فِي كِتَابٍ}. The second: it is a conjunction to «مثقالُ», and on this {إِلاَّ فِي كِتَابٍ} is a confirmation of the negation in «لا يَعْزُبُ», as if he said: "but it is in a clear Book."

Qatāda and al-Aʿmash read, and it was also transmitted from Abū ʿAmr and Nāfiʿ, with fatḥa on both rāʾs. There are two explanations for it: the first, that it is the «لا» of absolute denial (lā al-tabriʾa) and its noun is built along with it, with the khabar being His saying {إِلاَّ فِي كِتَابٍ}. The second: a conjunction to «ذَرَّةٍ». It was given in Yūnus that Ḥamza read with fatḥa on the rāʾ of «أصغر» and «أكبر», and here he agreed on the nominative. The discussion there was given at length. al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why is it not permissible to conjoin «ولا أصغرُ» to «مثقال», and «ولا أكبرَ» to «ذَرَّة»? I say: the particle of exception prevents that, unless you make the pronoun in «عنه» refer to the unseen (al-ghayb) and make «الغيب» a name for hidden things before they are written in the Tablet; for their being recorded in the Tablet is a kind of coming out from behind the veil, in the sense that nothing separates from the unseen and nothing slips from it except as written in the Tablet." The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "This interpretation is not needed if we make the Book not the Preserved Tablet."

Zayd ibn ʿAlī read with kasra on the rāʾ of «أصغر» and «أكبر», and it is very problematic. It was analysed on the basis that both are in the intention of iḍāfa, since the original is "nor its smallest nor its greatest", and what is a diptote, when annexed, becomes genitive in the position of the genitive; then the muḍāf ilayhi was omitted and its meaning intended, so the muḍāf was left as it was. It has parallels, such as their saying:

3711 - ... between my two forearms and the brow of the lion (... بين ذراعَيْ وجَبْهَةِ الأسَدِ)

and [his saying]:

3712 - O Taym of ʿAdī ... ... (يا تَيْمَ عَدِيٍّ ...)

with a disagreement. A distinction may be made: that there something indicates the omitted element in wording, unlike here. Some rejected this analysis because of the presence of «مِنْ», since an afʿal form, whenever annexed, does not combine with «مِنْ». That was answered in two ways. The first: that «مِنْ» is not attached to the afʿal but to an omitted element by way of explication, because when the muḍāf ilayhi was omitted the muḍāf became vague, and so it was clarified by «مِنْ» and its genitive noun, that is: "I mean from that." The second: that with the muḍāf ilayhi implied it is intended to be discarded, and that is why «مِنْ» was brought. This is indicated by the fact that explicit iḍāfa has occurred along with «مِنْ». The poet said: 3713 - We, in planting date-palm shoots, are more knowing than we are of galloping the steeds in the dark (نحن بغَرْسِ الوَدَي أَعْلَمُنا ... مِنَّا بركضِ الجيادِ في السُّدَفِ)

It was analysed in these two ways: either attachment to an omitted element, or the intention of discarding the muḍāf ilayhi. I say: this is like their need to interpret the combination of «أل» and «مِنْ» with afʿal, as in his saying:

3714 - And I am not the more numerous of them in pebbles ... (ولستُ بالأكثرِ منهم حَصَىً ...)

These are explanations of anomaly, from which no more is sought than that, so let one be content with the like of it.

semin-durr:4-4.t: His saying: {لِّيَجْزِيَ}: there are several explanations. The first: that it is attached to «لا يَعْزُب». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is attached to the meaning of «لا يَعْزُب», that is: 'He keeps count of that in order to repay'", and it is good; or to His saying «لتَأْتِيَنَّكم»; or to the governor in His saying {إِلاَّ فِي كِتَابٍ}, that is: "except that it is established in a clear Book, in order to repay." The two readings of «مُعاجزين» were given in al-Ḥajj.

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {أَلِيمٌ}: Ibn Kathīr and Ḥafṣ read «أليمٌ» nominative here and in al-Jāthiya. The rest read it genitive. The nominative is on the basis that it is an adjective of «عذاب», and the genitive on the basis that it is an adjective of «رِجْز». However, Makkī considered the nominative reading weak and remote, saying: "because al-rijz is the punishment, so the implied form would become: 'a painful punishment from punishment', and this meaning is not firmly grounded." He said: "The preferred reading is the genitive of «أليم» because it is sounder in the implied form and the meaning, since its implied form is: 'for them is a punishment of a painful punishment', that is, this kind among the kinds of punishment, because some punishment is more painful than other." I say: Makkī's statement has been answered: al-rijz is punishment in the general sense, as if it were said to them: "this kind of punishment is of the genus of punishment." Abū al-Baqāʾ seems to have noticed this when he said: "and with the nominative it is an adjective of «عذاب», and al-rijz is punishment in the general sense."

His saying: «والذين سَعَوْا»: two explanations are possible. The clearer: that it is a mubtadaʾ, with «أولئك» and what follows as its khabar. The second: that it is conjoined to «الذين» before it, that is: "and He repays those who strove", with the following «أولئك» resumptive, and the preceding «أولئك» and what is within its scope parenthetical between the two conjoined elements.

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {وَيَرَى الذين أُوتُواْ العلم}: there are two explanations. The first: that it is conjoined to «ليَجْزِيَ». al-Zamakhsharī said: "that is, 'and in order that those given knowledge may know, at the coming of the Hour'." I say: he restricted it with his words "at the coming of the Hour" only because he attached «ليجزيَ» to «لتأتينَّكم», and built this upon it; and it is one of the finest arrangements. The second: that it is resumptive, informing about them thus. «الذي أُنْزِلَ» is the first object, «هو» is the separating pronoun (faṣl), and «الحقَّ» is the second object, because the seeing is that of knowing.

Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «الحقُ» nominative as the khabar of «هو», the sentence being in the position of the second object; this is the dialect of Tamīm, who make the pronoun that is a faṣl a mubtadaʾ. And «مِنْ رَبِّك» is a ḥāl according to both readings.

His saying: «ويَهْدِي»: there are several explanations. The first: that it is resumptive. There are two possibilities for its agent: the clearer, that it is the pronoun of «الذي أُنْزِل»; the second, the pronoun of the name of Allah, and this is disturbed by His saying «إلى صراط العزيز», since if it were so, it would have been said: «إلى صراطه». This is answered: that it is an iltifāt (shift), and a bringing out of the pronoun as an overt noun to alert to His being described by them, between the two attributes.

The second of the explanations given: that it is conjoined to the position of «الحقَّ», with «أَنْ» implied along with it, its implied form being: "it is the truth and the guidance."

The third: that it is conjoined to «الحق», a verb conjoined to a noun because it is interpreted as one, like His saying the Exalted {صَافَّاتٍ وَيَقْبِضْنَ} [al-Mulk: 19], that is: "and gripping", just as a noun is conjoined to a verb because the verb has its meaning. Like the poet's saying:

3715 - And I found him one day destroying his enemy, and a sea of giving that makes the crossers light (فأَلْفَيْتُه يوماً يُبير عدوَّه ... وبحرَ عطاءٍ يستخِفُّ المعابرا)

as if it were said: "and that they may see it as the truth and as a guide."

The fourth: that «ويَهْدي» is a ḥāl from «الذي أُنْزِل», and a mubtadaʾ must be implied, that is: "and it guides", like:

3716 - ... ... I escaped, and I pledged (to them) Mālik (... نَجَوْتُ وأَرْهَنُهُمْ مالِكا)

and it is very rare.

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {إِذَا مُزِّقْتُمْ}: «إذا» is accusative by an implied verb, that is: "you will be raised and repaid at the time of your being torn to pieces", as indicated by {إِنَّكُمْ لَفِي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ}.

It is not permissible that the governor be «يُنَبِّئكم», because the informing does not occur at that time; nor «خَلْقٍ جديدٍ», because what follows «إنَّ» does not act on what precedes it; though one who is liberal about adverbs permitted it. This is if we make «إذا» a pure adverb. If we make it conditional, its apodosis is implied, that is "you will be raised", and that is the governor of «إذا» according to the majority of grammarians.

al-Zajjāj and al-Naḥḥās allowed it to be governed by «مُزِّقْتُمْ». Ibn ʿAṭiyya made this an error and a corruption of the meaning. The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "It is neither an error nor a corruption. There is disagreement over the governor in the conditional «إذا», and we showed in 'Sharḥ al-Tasḥīl' that the sound view is that its governor is the protasis verb, like its sisters among the conditional nouns." I say: but the majority hold the opposite. Then the Shaykh said: "The conditional sentence may be governed by «يُنَبِّئُكم», because it means: 'he tells you, when you are torn to pieces: you will be raised'. Then He confirmed that by His saying {إِنَّكُمْ لَفِي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ}. It is also possible that {إِنَّكُمْ لَفِي خَلْقٍ} is the suspension (taʿlīq) of «يُنَبِّئكم», filling the place of the two objects; and were it not for the lām, «إنَّ» would have had fatḥa. On this the conditional sentence is parenthetical. A group denied suspension with aʿlama and its chapter, but the sound view is that it is permissible. He said:

3717 - Beware, for I have been told that you are the one who will be repaid for what you strive for, so you will be happy or wretched (حَذارِ فقد نُبِّئْتُ إنكَ لَلَّذيْ ... ستُجْزَى بما تَسْعَى فتسعدَ أو تَشْقَى)

Zayd ibn ʿAlī read it with the hamza replaced by a yāʾ. And from him «يُنْبِئُكم», from anbaʾa on the pattern of akrama.

«مُمَزَّقٌ» has two explanations. The first: that it is a noun of verbal action (ism maṣdar), which is the rule for everything above three radicals, that is: its maṣdar, its time and its place come on the pattern of its passive participle, that is, "every tearing". The second: that it is an adverb of place; al-Zamakhsharī said this, that is: "every place of tearing, of the graves and the bellies of wild beasts and birds." Among examples of mufaʿʿal coming in the sense of tafʿīl is the saying:

3718 - Do you not know my composing of rhymes? Neither are they feeble nor borrowed (ألَمْ تَعْلَمْ مُسَرَّحِيَ القوافِيْ ... فلا عِيَّاً بهنَّ ولا اجْتِلابا)

that is, my "tasrīḥ" (releasing). And al-tamzīq is rending and cutting up. It is said: a torn garment (thawb mumazzaq and mamzūq). It is also said: mazaqahu, so he is māziq and mazaq also. He said: 3719 - It reached me that they are tearing my honour ... (أتاني أنهم مَزِقُون عِرْضِيْ ...)

And al-Mumazzaq al-ʿAbdī — after whom al-Mumazzaq was named — said:

3720 - If I am to be eaten, then be the best of eaters; otherwise reach me before I am torn (فإنْ كنتُ مأكولاً فكن خيرَ آكلٍ ... وإلاَّ فأدْرِكْني ولَمَّا أُمَزَّقِ)

that is: before I am worn out and perish.

And «جديد» according to the Basrans has the sense of fāʿil; it is said jadda al-shayʾ, so it is jādd and jadīd; and according to the Kufans it has the sense of mafʿūl, from jadadtuhu, that is, "I cut it".

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {أفترى}: this is the hamza of interrogation. The hamzat al-waṣl was omitted because of it, and so this hamza is retained in continuation and in beginning. From this verse al-Jāḥiẓ drew evidence that speech is of three kinds: true, false, and neither true nor false. The way the evidence indicates the third kind is that His saying {أَم بِهِ جِنَّةٌ} cannot be false, because it is the counterpart of falsehood, and the counterpart of a thing is other than it; nor can it be true, because they did not believe it; so a third kind is established. It was answered that the meaning is: "or has he not forged it?" but it was expressed by their saying {أَم بِهِ جِنَّةٌ} because the madman has no forging.

The apparent view concerning this «أم» is that it is connected (muttaṣila), because it is implied as "which of the two things", and is answered by one of them, as if it were said: "which of the two is the case: his forging a lie, or his being mad?" It does no harm that a sentence follows it, because the sentence is interpreted as a single word, as in the saying:

3721 - I do not care whether a billy-goat bleated in the rough ground, or a base man slandered me behind my back (لا أُبالي أَنَبَّ بالحَزْنِ تَيْسٌ ... أم جفاني بظهرِ غَيْبٍ لئيمُ)

and like it the saying of another:

3722 - By your life, I do not know — though I might have known — whether it is Shuʿayth ibn Sahm or Shuʿayth ibn Minqar (لَعَمْرُك ما أدْري وإنْ كنتُ دارياً ... شُعَيْثُ ابن سَهْمٍ أم شُعَيْثُ ابنُ منقرِ)

«ابن منقر» is a khabar, not an adjective. Thus one of them recited it, citing it as evidence that it is a sentence; and in it the tanwīn is omitted from what precedes «ابن», though it is not an attribute. You know what I alluded to here from Sūrat al-Tawba.

semin-durr:9-9.t:
His saying: {أَفَلَمْ}: here there are the two well-known opinions: al-Zamakhsharī implied "Were they blind, so they did not see?", while others claim that the hamza is advanced before the conjunction.

His saying «من السماء»: an explication (bayān) of the relative noun, and so it is attached to an omitted element. It may also be a ḥāl, and then it is likewise attached to it. It was said: and there is an omitted ḥāl, its implied form being: "Do they not see such-and-such subdued under Our power, or encompassing them?" Then He said: «إنْ نَشَأْ».

His saying: «إنْ نَشَأْ»: al-Akhawān read «يَشَأْ ... يَخْسِفْ ... يُسْقِطْ» with a yāʾ in the three. The rest read with the nūn of majesty in them, and both are clear. al-Kisāʾī assimilated the fāʾ into the bāʾ, and people considered this weak because the stronger was assimilated into the weaker. al-Fārisī said: "That is not permissible, because the bāʾ is weaker in sound than the fāʾ, so it is not assimilated into it, although the bāʾ is assimilated into it in «اضربْ فلاناً», just as the bāʾ is assimilated into the mīm in your saying «اضربْ مالِكاً», though the mīm is not assimilated into the bāʾ as in «اضمُمْ بكراً», because the bāʾ falls below the mīm in lacking nasalisation (ghunna)." al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is not strong"; but this should not be said, because it is mutawātir.

His saying: «يا جِبالُ»: quoted by an implied saying. Then, if you wish, you may imply it as a maṣdar, being a badal of «فَضْلاً» by way of explaining it, as if it were said: "We gave him a favour: Our saying 'O mountains'"; and if you wish you may imply a verb, in which case you have two possibilities: if you wish you may make it a badal of «آتَيْنا», and if you wish you may make it resumptive.

His saying: «أَوِّبِيْ»: the majority read it with fatḥa on the hamza and shadda on the wāw, an imperative from taʾwīb, which is repeating (tarjīʿ). It was also said: glorification (tasbīḥ) in the language of Abyssinia. The doubling may be for intensification. The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) preferred that it be for making transitive; he said: "because they explained it as 'repeat the glorification with him'." But there is no proof, because that is an explanation of meaning. Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, Qatāda and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read «أُوْبي» with ḍamma on the hamza and a quiescent wāw, an imperative from āba yaʾūbu, that is: "return with him in glorification."

His saying: «والطيرَ»: the majority read it accusative, and there are several explanations. The first: that it is conjoined to the position of «جبالُ», because it is accusative in the implied sense. The second: that it is an object of accompaniment; al-Zajjāj said this. It was rejected on the ground that «معه» comes before it, and the governor does not require more than one object of accompaniment, except by badal or conjunction; one does not say «جاء زيدٌ مع بكرٍ مع عمروٍ». I say: their disagreement over the governor's requiring two ḥāls would require its permissibility here. The third: that it is conjoined to «فضْلاً»; al-Kisāʾī said this. A muḍāf must then be omitted, its implied form being: "We gave him favour and the glorification of the birds." The fourth: that it is accusative by an implied verb, that is: "and We subjected the birds to him"; Abū ʿAmr said this.

al-Sulamī, al-Aʿraj, Yaʿqūb, Abū Nawfal, Abū Yaḥyā and ʿĀṣim in one transmission read «والطيرُ» nominative. There are several explanations: a conjunction to the form of the word «جبالُ». The following saying was recited:

3723 - O Zayd and al-Ḍaḥḥāk, travel on, for you two have passed the shelter of the road (ألا يا زيدُ والضَّحاكُ سِيْرا ... فقد جاوَزْتُما خَمَرَ الطريقِ)

in both ways (nominative and accusative). Regarding the conjunction of a noun with «أل» to a vocative that carries ḍamma, there are three positions. The second: its conjunction to the latent pronoun in «أوِّبي»; this is permissible because of the separation by the adverbial. The third: nominative as a mubtadaʾ with an implied khabar, that is: "and the mountains likewise", that is, made to return in praise.

His saying: «وألَنَّا»: conjoined to «آتَيْنا», and it is part of the favour.

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying: {أَنِ اعمل}: there are two explanations for it. The clearer: that it is a maṣdar particle, on the omission of the preposition, that is: "so that". The second, said by al-Ḥawfī and others, is that it is explicative (mufassira). This was rejected on the ground that its condition is that something with the meaning of "saying" must precede, and nothing preceded except «أَلَنَّا». Some excused this by implying something with the meaning of saying, that is: "and We commanded him: Make…", and no necessity calls for that.

It was also read «صابغاتٍ» because of the ghayn. Its explanation has been given in Luqmān at «وأَسْبَغَ».

semin-durr:12-12.t:
His saying: {وَلِسُلَيْمَانَ الريح}: the majority read it accusative by an implied verb, that is: "and We subjected the wind to Sulaymān." Abū Bakr read it nominative as a mubtadaʾ, the khabar being in the preceding preposition and its genitive noun, or omitted. Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed that it be an agent — he means of the preposition and its genitive noun — but it is not strong, for lack of reliance (on a preceding element). Another had agreed with him in al-Anbiyāʾ.

The majority read «الريحَ» in the singular. al-Ḥasan, Abū Ḥaywa and Khālid ibn Ilyās read «الرياحَ» in the plural. It was given in al-Anbiyāʾ that al-Ḥasan reads with the accusative as well, while here nothing was transmitted from him to that effect.

His saying: «غُدُوُّها شَهْرٌ»: mubtadaʾ and khabar. A muḍāf must be omitted, that is: "its morning journey is a month's journey" or "the extent of its morning journey is a month." If it were accusative it would be permissible, except that it has not been read thus, as far as I know.

Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «غَدْوَتُها ورَوْحَتُها», in the form of a single occurrence. The sentence is either resumptive or in the position of a ḥāl.

His saying: «مَنْ يَعْمَلُ»: it may be nominative as a mubtadaʾ, its khabar in the preceding preposition and its genitive noun, that is: "among the jinn are those who work"; or it may be in the position of accusative by an implied verb, that is: "and We subjected to him those who work." And «من الجنّ» is attached to this implied verb, or to an omitted element as a ḥāl or an explication. And «بإذن» is a ḥāl, that is: "made easy by the permission of his Lord." And al-idhn is a maṣdar annexed to its agent. It was also read «ومَنْ يُزِغْ» with ḍamma on the yāʾ, from azāgha, with its object omitted, that is: "and whoever makes himself deviate", that is, inclines it. And «مِنْ عذاب»: «مِنْ» marks the starting point or is partitive.

semin-durr:13-13.t:
And {يَعْمَلُونَ لَهُ مَا يَشَآءُ}: it explains His saying «مَنْ يعمل». And «مِنْ مَحاريب» is an explication (bayān) of «ما يَشاء».

His saying: «كالجوابِ»: Ibn Kathīr read it retaining the yāʾ of «الجوابي» in continuation and in pause. Abū ʿAmr and Warsh retain it in continuation and drop it in pause. The rest drop it in both cases. And «كالجواب» is an adjective of «جِفان». «الجِفان» is the plural of «جَفْنَة». «الجوابي» is the plural of «جابِيَة», like ḍāriba and ḍawāribu. «الجابية» is a great basin, so named because water is gathered (yujbā) into it. Attributing the act to it is figurative, because it is gathered in it, as it is said khābiya for what is stored (yukhabbaʾu) in it. The poet said:

3724 - With bowls that visit our gathering, of fat slices of hump when the north wind blew; like basins, never ceasing to be filled, for the hospitality of guests or of the one at death's door (بجِفانٍ تَعْتَرِي نادِيَنا ... مِنْ سَدِيْفٍ حين هاجَ الصِّنَّبِرْ / كالجوابي لاتِني مُتْرَعَةً ... لِقِرى الأضيافِ أو للمحتضِرْ)

And al-Aʿshā said:

3725 - A bowl removed blame from the family of al-Muḥallaq, like a basin of the Iraqi stream, overflowing (نَفَى الذَّمَّ عن آلِ المُحَلَّقِ جَفْنَةٌ ... كجابِيَةِ السَّيْحِ العِراقيِّ تَفْهَقُ)

And al-Afwah said:

3726 - And cauldrons like firm hills, and bowls like basins, filled to the brim (وقُدُوْرٍ كالرُّبا راسِيَةٍ ... وجِفانٍ كالجَوابي مُتْرَعَهْ)

His saying: «شُكْراً»: several explanations are possible. The first: that it is a direct object, that is: "perform obedience". Prayer and the like are called thanks (shukr) because they fill its place. The second: that it is a maṣdar from the meaning of «اعْمَلوا», as if it were said: "give thanks, a thanks, by your work", or "work the work of gratitude". The third: that it is an object of purpose (mafʿūl li-ajlihi), that is: "for the sake of thanks". The fourth: that it is a maṣdar occupying the position of a ḥāl, that is: "thankfully". The fifth: that it is accusative by an implied verb of its own wording, its implied form being: "and give thanks, a thanks". The sixth: that it is an adjective of the maṣdar of «اعْمَلوا», its implied form being: "work a work of thanks", that is, possessing thanks.

His saying: «وقليلٌ»: an advanced khabar. And «من عبادِيْ» is an adjective of it, and «الشَّكورُ» is the mubtadaʾ.

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying: {تَأْكُلُ}: either a ḥāl or resumptive. As for «مِنْسَأْتَه»: Ibn Dhakwān read it with a quiescent hamza; Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr with a pure alif; and the rest with a hamza carrying fatḥa.

«المِنْسَأَةُ» is the staff, a noun of instrument from nasaʾahu, that is, "he delayed it", like «المِكْسَحَة» and «المِكْنَسَة». With the hamza it is the dialect of Tamīm, and this was recited:

3727 - Is it on account of a rope, may you have no father, that you struck it with a staff, that your rope has dragged along ropes? (أمِنْ أَجْلِ حَبْلٍ لا أَباك ضَرَبْتَه ... بمِنْسَأَةٍ قد جَرَّ حَبْلُكَ أَحْبُلا)

With the alif it is the dialect of the Hijaz. And this was recited:

3728 - When you creep along on the staff from old age, then play and flirtation have drawn far from you (إذا دَبَبْتَ على المِنْساة مِنْ كِبَرٍ ... فقد تباعَدَ عنك اللهوُ والغَزَلُ)

As for the hamza with fatḥa, it is the original, because derivation indicates and attests to it, and the fatḥa is for the pattern mifʿala, like miknasa. As for its being quiescent, there are two explanations. The first: that he replaced the hamza with an alif, as Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr replaced it (this will come), then replaced this alif with a hamza in the dialect of those who say «العَأْلَم» and «الخَأْتَم», and the saying:

3729 - And Khindif is the head of this ʿaʾlam (the world) (وخِنْدِفٌ هامَةُ هذا العَأْلَمِ)

Ibn Mālik mentioned it. I do not know what led him to this: how can it be held that he fled from something and then returned to it? Moreover, they stated explicitly that when a hamza is substituted for an alif: if that alif has an origin, this hamza is given the vowel of the origin of the alif. Abū al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUṣfūr recited on this:

3730 - The ostriches of the Banū Ṣafwān fled, rushing off in a hurry ... (وَلَّى نَعامُ بني صفوانَ زَوْزَأَةً ...)

He said: the origin is «زَوْزاة», and the origin of this is «زَوْزَوَة»; when it was replaced from the alif by a hamza, he gave it the vowel of the wāw. Having known this, this alif should have been replaced by a hamza with fatḥa, because it is from a vowelled origin, namely the hamza with fatḥa, and so it would return to the first; and this is not said. The second: that he made the fatḥa quiescent for lightness, and the fatḥa has been made quiescent in places whose notice and attestations have been given.
